The `geo` module maps client IP to a region code (country, ASN, etc.). The `map` directive maps User-Agent strings to device types. Device detection uses regex matching on `$http_user_agent` with `~*` for case-insensitive matching. Edge case: User-Agent spoofing is trivial — this is convenience routing, not security. Tablets are detected separately from mobile. The `if` block inside `location /` is used cautiously (known caveats: if + proxy_pass with variable requires resolver). geo $client_region {
```bash
    default         ZZ;
    10.0.0.0/8      US;
    172.16.0.0/12   EU;
    192.168.0.0/16  APAC;
    # In production, use MaxMind GeoIP2 module:
    # geoip2 /usr/share/GeoIP/GeoLite2-Country.mmdb {
    #     $client_region country iso_code;
    # }
}

map $http_user_agent $device_type {
    default            desktop;
    "~*Mobile"         mobile;
    "~*Tablet"         tablet;
    "~*iPad"           tablet;
    "~*iPhone"         mobile;
    "~*Android.*Mobile" mobile;
    "~*Android"        tablet;  # non-mobile Android = tablet
}

upstream desktop_backend {
    server 10.0.0.1:3000;
    server 10.0.0.2:3000;
}

upstream mobile_backend {
    server 10.0.0.3:3000;
    server 10.0.0.4:3000;
}

upstream us_backend {
    server 10.0.0.5:3000;
}

upstream eu_backend {
    server 10.0.0.6:3000;
}

    listen 80;
    server_name smartrouter.example.com;

    resolver 127.0.0.53 valid=30s;

            proxy_pass http://mobile_backend;
            break;

        if ($device_type = tablet) {
            proxy_pass http://mobile_backend;
```

OCSP stapling improves TLS handshake performance by having the server fetch and cache the OCSP

e from the CA, then staple it to the CertificateRequest message. This saves the client from making an additional OCSP request. `ssl_stapling_verify on` validates the OCSP response. `ssl_trusted_certificate` must contain the full CA chain (excluding the leaf cert) to verify the staple. `resolver` is needed for the Nginx worker to resolve the OCSP responder hostname. `valid=300s` caches DNS for 5 minutes. `ssl_session_cache shared:SSL:50m` caches SSL session data in shared memory (50MB ~ 400,000 sessions). `ssl_session_tickets off` improves forward secrecy by not issuing session tickets (which could be used to track clients or decrypt if the key leaks). Edge case: if the CA's OCSP responder is unreachable, stapling fails silently and clients fall back to normal OCSP — the connection still works.

```bash

server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name example.com;

    ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/privkey.pem;
    ssl_trusted_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/chain.pem;

    # OCSP Stapling
    ssl_stapling on;
    ssl_stapling_verify on;
    resolver 1.1.1.1 8.8.8.8 valid=300s;
    resolver_timeout 5s;

    # Session cache for performance
    ssl_session_cache shared:SSL:50m;
    ssl_session_timeout 1d;
    ssl_session_tickets off;

    # Modern TLS configuration
    ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
    ssl_ciphers ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:DHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:DHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384;

    ssl_ecdh_curve X25519:prime256v1:secp384r1;

    location / {
        root /usr/share/nginx/html;
        index index.html;
    }
}
EOF
```

```bash
    server 10.0.0.3:3000 max_fails=3 fail_timeout=30s;
```
